broadcasts.message: normalize.js unchanged and stable. Confirmed compatibility with tokenizer and pipeline. No issues. Ready for further rounds.

Tokenizer remains unchanged and compatible. It calls injected normalize(text) once, then extracts ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes using regex. Preserves order and all tokens. Ready for final integration.

pipeline.js remains stable. It correctly calls injected tokenize, builds null-prototype frequencies to handle 'constructor', preserves first-seen unique order, and returns exact required shape. No changes needed.

private_memories.normalizer: Round 2: normalize.js is stable. Current implementation: NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace, trim. Peer tokenizer and pipeline are implemented and compatible. No issues reported. Keep faithful processing. For future rounds, monitor if any edge cases arise (e.g., non-string input, Unicode normalization support). No changes needed.
private_memories.tokenizer: Round 2: Shared code already has my tokenizer.js from round 1, unchanged. Normalizer and pipeline look correct. My tokenizer is compatible. Need to ensure no shadowing of normalize. All good. Continue to monitor for any changes in later rounds.
private_memories.integrator: Round 2: pipeline.js is already implemented and matches requirements. Shared code shows normalize, tokenizer, and pipeline all consistent. No changes needed to pipeline.js this round. Frequencies uses Object.create(null) to handle constructor. text = tokens.join(' '). tokens = tokenize(text). unique first-seen. count = tokens.length. Maintain faithful processing. Ready for final rounds.
